verdict.root_cause: About three minutes before onset, platform automation attached a traffic-shaping container to cart-service's network namespace applying a fixed 300ms egress delay with zero jitter on eth0 [tr_3260771d0685]. Every Redis round-trip cartservice makes therefore pays ~300ms of pure wait: traces show HGET/HMSET client-span self-times tightly banded at ~301-305ms while the cartservice gRPC handler self-time stays sub-millisecond, and server-span duration scales with the number of Redis operations (GetCart ~302ms with one HGET, AddItem ~603ms with HGET+HMSET) [tr_0ea671ada1bb]. The same shaped namespace also delays cartservice's replies, so callers absorb an extra ~300ms each (frontend ~302-306ms over the callee, checkoutservice ~908-921ms), explaining why frontend, checkoutservice and loadgenerator alerted seconds later while staying functionally healthy [tr_0ea671ada1bb][tr_a95591494649]. Nothing is erroring or exhausted: cartservice keeps serving and logging normal cart operations with no error or connection-failure lines [tr_de406478f270] and no span carries an error status [tr_0ea671ada1bb]. Detaching the shaping container restores service.
verdict.reasoning: The change record supplies a proximate act with a quantitative prediction - constant 300ms egress delay, zero jitter, on cartservice's network namespace, ~3 minutes before onset [tr_3260771d0685] - and the traces match it in detail: near-constant ~300ms with negligible spread, charged per Redis round-trip rather than per RPC, localized entirely in the Redis client child spans while handler self-time stays sub-millisecond [tr_0ea671ada1bb]. That pattern discriminates against competitors: queueing would widen the distribution and grow; application CPU/GC/lock contention would appear in handler self-time; a Redis outage or wrong REDIS_ADDR would produce connection errors, and the logs contain none [tr_de406478f270]. Onset is a step change (healthy at 18:11-18:17, degraded from 18:23:17) consistent with an attachment event [tr_0ea671ada1bb]. Blame sits on cartservice rather than the co-alerting callers: their other dependencies remain at 0-20ms and frontend's error ratio stays under 1% [tr_a95591494649][tr_0ea671ada1bb], so their symptoms follow from cartservice's shaped path. The class is dependency_latency because the failure is waiting, not a wrong value or an exhausted resource; the shaping attachment is how it started and detaching it - a reversible operation, per the earlier attach/remove cycle - is the fix [tr_3260771d0685]. Both cartservice metric dispatches returned zero samples in incident and baseline windows [tr_7026064abf3e], so metrics neither support nor contradict this.
open_questions: Whether the shaping container is still attached or has already been detached as in the earlier cycle [tr_3260771d0685]; no latency or throughput metric was ever queried for cartservice, so the step is confirmed only from sampled traces [tr_7026064abf3e].
Why cartservice span-metrics (calls_total) are unpopulated even pre-incident - a separate instrumentation gap that blinded the metrics channel [tr_7026064abf3e].

The nature of frontend's small but genuinely new error population, and the exact accounting for checkoutservice's ~908-921ms (roughly three increments), neither of which the sampled evidence resolves [tr_a95591494649][tr_0ea671ada1bb].

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart itself became slow, adding ~300ms per operation, with the shaping container coincidental.
alternatives.why_not: Demoted by the near-zero variance of the delay, by a change matching that exact figure landing on cartservice's namespace 3 minutes before onset, and by callers absorbing their own extra ~300ms on the return path, which store-side slowness would not produce [tr_0ea671ada1bb][tr_3260771d0685]. Redis was never inspected directly, so it is not eliminated.

proposal.expected_effect: After reverting cartservice to its recorded prior configuration and recreating the container, traces should show Redis HGET/HMSET client spans fall from the ~301-305ms band back to the pre-onset 0.1-0.6ms range, cartservice server spans back to ~0.4-1.5ms with no ~300ms-per-Redis-op scaling, and checkoutservice's GetCart/EmptyCart client spans down from ~908-921ms to single-digit ms. Frontend error ratio should return to its zero baseline. Cartservice's own calls_total series is empty in both windows, so traces are the only confirming channel.
proposal.if_wrong: If post-recreate traces still band Redis ops at ~300ms, the shaping lives in the network namespace and not in cartservice's recorded config; the real fix is detaching the shaping container, which is outside this system's actions - withdraw and escalate. If a pre-action trace query already shows healthy sub-millisecond Redis spans, the shaping was already detached as in the earlier cycle and the recreate is pure cost; this check should gate the action.
proposal.risk: Container recreate drops in-flight cart calls, converting a latency-only, error-free incident into brief hard failures for frontend and checkoutservice, and discards cartservice in-process state. If the diagnosis is wrong the outage is added for no benefit, and reverting config could also undo unrelated settings recorded in the same prior state.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice for the duration of the recreate; its inbound callers frontend and checkoutservice see resets, and loadgenerator sees the resulting request failures. Redis (redis-cart) sees a brief connection drop and reconnect.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Multiple services alerted within seconds spanning cart, frontend, and checkout, plus the load generator — that is a user-facing path degrading, not a single quiet warning. No open incident to attribute it to, so it warrants investigation with cartservice as a likely shared dependency.
